behavioral_notes.observation: Public /profile/user/<id> and /profile/avatar/<id> enforce a code-only privacy policy invisible to metadata: a user always sees their own profile; otherwise the target must be website_published (else 'This profile is private!'), and the requesting user's karma must be >= request.website.karma_profile_min (default 150) or access is denied 'Not have enough karma to view other users' profile'. Avatars are streamed sudo only when the target is published AND karma > 0 (i.e. has participated in forum/eLearning); the image field is whitelisted to image/avatar 128/256 else Forbidden. This is the visibility gate the whole public-profile layer rests on.

/profile/users builds a karma leaderboard over res.users filtered by karma>1 AND website_published. Default order is karma DESC, id DESC; with group_by=week/month it instead calls res.users._get_user_ids_ranked_by_karma(), a raw SQL aggregation summing gamification_karma_tracking.(new_value-old_value) over the period (LEFT JOIN tracking, GROUP BY user, ORDER BY karma gain DESC). Absolute positions come from _get_karma_position / _get_tracking_karma_gain_position (window-function row_number over the same domain), and the signed-in user is appended with their real position even when off the page. top3_users feeds the podium. None of this ranking math is derivable from metadata.

website_profile widens res.users self-readable/writable fields (exposes 'karma' for read; allows self-edit of country_id/city/website/website_description/website_published) and re-declares gamification.badge with website.published.mixin so badges become individually publishable to the public page. The karma ledger and rank engine live in gamification: /profile/ranks_badges reads gamification.karma.rank (sudo, order karma_min DESC) and published gamification.badge (sorted by granted_users_count). Rank assignment is gamification.res.users._recompute_rank, mapping karma to the highest karma.rank whose karma_min is met and storing next_rank_id (the rank above) that the 'next rank' progress card renders. The publish flag and rank thresholds are the levers the public reputation page exposes.

/profile/send_validation_email sends a tokenised mail (validation_email template) via _send_profile_validation_email; the token is a daily-rotating SHA-256 over a secret ir.config_parameter 'website_profile.uuid' + user_id + email. /profile/validate_email calls _process_profile_validation_token, and only if the token matches AND the user's karma is still 0 does it write karma = VALIDATION_KARMA_GAIN (3). This one-time email-confirmation reward and its token scheme exist only in code; session flags validation_email_sent/done drive the UI banner, and portal.py resets validation_email_sent when the partner's email changes.

Ships 5 JS files, 1 XML template, 1 OWL component (ProfileDialog) and 4 website public.interactions registry adds (profile_editor, its .edit variant for the builder iframe, next_rank_card, profile_validation). Assets target web.assets_frontend (6), website.assets_inside_builder_iframe (1) and web.assets_tests (1); the editor interaction is excluded from the public bundle via ('remove', '**/*.edit.js'). The next-rank card and the in-page profile editor (with file_handler image upload + html_editor description) are the rich client widgets layered on the gamification data.

information_flows: depends: html_editor (rich description editing), website_partner (partner-website link), gamification (karma/ranks/badges)
side-effect: /profile/user/<id> -> visibility gated by website_published + viewer karma >= website.karma_profile_min
side-effect: /profile/users -> leaderboard via res.users._get_user_ids_ranked_by_karma (SQL over gamification.karma.tracking)
consumed-by: website_forum, website_slides (public reputation pages + karma redirection)

value_streams: Reputation loop: participate (earn karma) -> publish profile -> climb leaderboard / rank up -> badges & next-rank motivation surfaced publicly
organization: website.group_website_restricted_editor (manage karma ranks on the website)
policies: privacy: a profile is visible to others only if website_published AND viewer karma >= website.karma_profile_min (default 150)
avatar served publicly only for published users with karma > 0
self-edit limited to own privacy/profile fields (SELF_WRITEABLE_FIELDS); admin may edit others
email validation grants karma (3) only once, when karma == 0, via a daily-rotating SHA-256 token
metrics: karma totals and per-period karma gain (leaderboard position)
badge counts per user (badge_ids) and granted_users_count per badge

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_profile is a community profile/reputation layer that mediates member visibility and standing rather than producing a good (chain) or matching buyers and sellers (shop). Per Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a value-network configuration: its value is the network of published members and the karma/rank/badge reputation that links them, exposed through public /profile pages, a karma leaderboard and per-member rank progression. It underpins the community front-ends (forum, eLearning/website_slides), so it is the primary member-facing activity of that engagement stack -- an audience-building / community-marketing capability under APQC 3.0 Market and Sell (build and manage the customer/member community), as distinct from the gamification engine it consumes, which is the HR-support (7.0) reward machinery.

standard_capabilities: public user profile pages with avatar, bio (html_editor) and stats
karma/rank display with a motivational next-rank card
published badge catalog on the profile and /profile/ranks_badges page
member leaderboard with all-time and weekly/monthly karma-gain ranking and pagination
self-service profile editing and one-time email validation (karma reward)
privacy gating via website_published + per-website minimum karma to view others
typical_fits: any website community surfacing member karma and badges
common_gaps: custom profile fields or layout beyond name/bio/location/badges
alternative reputation/scoring rules (karma point values are defined by consumer modules, not here)
richer privacy tiers beyond the single karma_profile_min threshold
leaderboard segmentation/filters beyond all-time / week / month
drive_hints: curl public: GET /profile/ranks_badges and /profile/users (published, karma>1 only)

open_questions: Exact karma point values that drive ranks/leaderboard are set by consumer modules (forum/website_slides), not website_profile.
How website_forum / website_slides extend the profile page (badge_category filters, extra tabs) beyond the base hooks.
Whether karma_profile_min is commonly retuned per deployment from its default of 150.
